response: Yes, screening or surveillance for primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with ultrasonography has been shown to improve the prognosis of patients. Regular ultrasonography screening can lead to earlier detection of HCC, often at an asymptomatic stage, when the tumor is smaller and more amenable to curative treatments such as surgical resection, liver transplantation, or ablation. This early detection can result in improved survival rates and outcomes for patients with HCC.
